question: Does explicitly passing information from a protein's physicochemical surface mesh into its residue graph yield compact representations that work across binding-affinity and enzyme-function tasks?

key_findings.claim: HoloProt is a directed surface-to-residue fusion architecture rather than a generic hierarchy learned from raw protein data.
key_findings.evidence: An MSMS triangulated surface carries curvature, charge, hydropathy, and donor features; surface-message embeddings are mean-pooled by residue identifier, concatenated to hand-engineered residue features, and processed by a second message-passing network. Only the final residue embeddings are globally summed.

key_findings.claim: Molecular superpixels compress a roughly 2,600-face surface into 20 clusters using a task-independent entropy-rate segmentation and summary statistics.
key_findings.evidence: The graph objective balances random-walk entropy and cluster size and is optimized submodularly. Each cluster is represented by mean, standard deviation, maximum, and minimum for every surface feature, with Wasserstein distances on adjacent clusters; all meshes are downsampled to about 2,600 faces and figures use k=20.

key_findings.claim: On PDBBind, HoloProt is strongest on the scaffold and 60%-identity splits but not uniformly on the hardest 30%-identity split.
key_findings.evidence: Across three runs on 4,709 complexes, the paper reports that HoloProt outperforms all baselines on scaffold and identity 60%. On identity 30%, its full-surface RMSE is 1.464 +/- 0.006 while the pocket-only Townshend ENN reports 1.429 +/- 0.042; the authors flag that pocket-only inputs simplify the task.

key_findings.claim: The enzyme result is parameter-efficient but not close in absolute accuracy to the top structural baseline.
key_findings.evidence: Full-surface and superpixel HoloProt achieve 77.8% and 78.9% accuracy with 0.64M parameters, versus 87.2% for Hermosilla et al. with 9.8M. A 5.2M HoloProt reaches only 79.2% without a hyperparameter search, so the 8.3-point gap cannot be attributed solely to parameter count.

key_findings.claim: Ablations show small, task-dependent fusion gains and weaken the claim that superpixels lose little or no information.
key_findings.evidence: At 30% identity, structure-only RMSE/Pearson/Spearman are 1.476/0.510/0.503, full HoloProt is 1.464/0.509/0.500, and superpixel HoloProt worsens to 1.491/0.491/0.482. For enzyme classification, however, surface-only is 28.6%, structure-only 74.2%, full 77.8%, and superpixels 78.9%.

key_findings.claim: The experimental comparison is constrained by heterogeneous protocols, incomplete sweeps, and substantial preprocessing.
key_findings.evidence: Enzyme baselines are copied from a prior paper; binding baselines use different training and input protocols; MaSIF and larger HoloProt variants lack full sweeps due to time or memory. Surface generation requires MSMS, Blender, APBS, PDB2PQR, multivalue, and DSSP, and Appendix Table 4 explicitly says missing superpixel-MPN results will be added later.

method.core_idea: Fuse local physicochemical surface geometry into residue-level protein representations through explicit cross-scale edges, with optional surface clustering for memory efficiency.
method.mechanism: Run a Weisfeiler-Lehman-style message-passing network on the surface mesh, mean-pool surface states belonging to each residue, concatenate them with residue/secondary-structure features, run a residue-graph MPN, and attach task-specific global heads; optionally replace mesh vertices with entropy-rate superpixels.
assumptions: A reliable experimental or predicted 3D structure is available for every protein.
A single static solvent-excluded surface and its handcrafted physicochemical features capture task-relevant interactions.
Residue identifiers correctly align every surface vertex to the residue graph.
Mean pooling preserves the useful distribution of surface patches around each residue.
Global protein and ligand embeddings are sufficient for affinity without explicit cross-molecular interaction geometry.
Twenty superpixels and uniform 2,600-face downsampling are adequate across proteins of very different sizes.

techniques.role: Transfers surface-node embeddings into the matching residue nodes.
Encodes both surface and residue graphs with neighborhood aggregation.
Clusters surface meshes into compact, balanced physicochemical regions.
Summarizes each surface region with four moments/extrema per feature.
Predicts affinity from separately pooled protein and ligand graphs.
Tests generalization away from homologous proteins or familiar ligand scaffolds.

evaluations.setting: PDBBind 2019 refined subset, 4,709 complexes, scaffold and 30%/60% sequence-identity splits
evaluations.result: Strongest reported method on scaffold and identity 60%; competitive but not best against the pocket-only ENN on identity 30%
evaluations.baseline: Sequence, surface, structure, and pocket-only affinity models

evaluations.setting: Enzyme Commission classification, 37,428 proteins across 384 EC labels
evaluations.result: 77.8% full surface and 78.9% superpixels with 0.64M parameters
evaluations.baseline: Sequence and structure encoders; best Hermosilla baseline is 87.2%

evaluations.result: Full fusion improves RMSE slightly over structure-only but not correlations; superpixels underperform both isolated scales
Structure 74.2%, surface 28.6%, full 77.8%, superpixels 78.9%, superpixel MPN 75.7%
evaluations.baseline: Individual scales and alternate superpixel encoding

evaluations.setting: Resource profile on a single NVIDIA 1080 Ti
evaluations.result: PDBBind HoloProt runs within 16h for 200 epochs; enzyme training is stopped after 24h at roughly 100-110 epochs
evaluations.baseline: Several adapted baselines require up to about 40h

limitations: Author-stated: the method requires existing or predicted protein structures, which are unavailable for many design variants.
Author-stated: precomputed molecular surfaces add a deployment bottleneck.
Affinity conflates Ki and Kd and concatenates global protein/ligand embeddings without modeling their bound pose or atom-level contacts.
Static structures omit conformational ensembles, uncertainty, solvent dynamics, and mutation-induced changes.
Baseline protocols and tuning budgets are heterogeneous, and some classification numbers are imported rather than rerun.
The enzyme top-line remains 8.3 accuracy points below the strongest baseline despite the 'close' characterization.
The public manuscript contains an explicitly unfinished ablation table and no statistical uncertainty for enzyme classification.
failure_modes: MSMS or electrostatics preprocessing fails on malformed, unusual, or very large structures.
Uniform face downsampling erases a small catalytic pocket or narrow channel.
Fixed-k superpixels merge distinct functional patches on large proteins or oversegment small ones.
Mean surface-to-residue pooling loses multimodal orientation and patch geometry.
A predicted apo structure differs from the ligand-bound conformation needed for affinity.
Global protein/ligand concatenation exploits dataset biases rather than physical interaction complementarity.
reusable_insights: Compare graph, surface, and fused models under one identical benchmark protocol and tuning budget.
Report gains relative to both parameter count and total preprocessing/training cost.
Adaptive surface coarsening should preserve pockets and quantify reconstruction of functional regions, not only downstream averages.
Cross-scale fusion benefits should be separated from extra features and extra parameters through matched ablations.
Binding-affinity models need pose-aware interaction tests and scaffold/protein joint holdouts.
Use ensembles or uncertainty when predicted structures replace experimental conformations.
open_questions: Can on-the-fly differentiable surfaces remove the preprocessing stack while retaining cross-scale benefits?
Would bidirectional, layerwise atom/residue/surface fusion outperform one-shot surface-to-residue mean pooling?
How should superpixel count adapt to protein size and functional-pocket density?
Do HoloProt features generalize to mutation effects, unseen folds, or experimentally measured prospective assays?
Can ligand-pose-aware cross-attention distinguish real binding physics from dataset shortcuts?
How robust is the representation to AlphaFold uncertainty and alternate conformations?

competitive_landscape.title: Fast End-to-End Learning on Protein Surfaces
competitive_landscape.difference: dMaSIF computes a differentiable surface point cloud and chemical/geometric features directly from atoms, avoiding the mesh and handcrafted preprocessing that HoloProt lists as a core limitation.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning from Protein Structure with Geometric Vector Perceptrons
competitive_landscape.difference: GVP-GNN carries scalar and vector features equivariantly for protein design and quality assessment; HoloProt uses scalar surface/residue message passing and explicit handcrafted surface fusion.

competitive_landscape.title: Protein Representation Learning by Geometric Structure Pretraining
competitive_landscape.difference: GearNet uses geometry-aware relational graphs plus self-supervised structure pretraining across tasks, while HoloProt is trained from scratch on each task and relies on surface preprocessing.

competitive_landscape.title: Surface-VQMAE: Vector-quantized Masked Auto-encoders on Molecular Surfaces
competitive_landscape.difference: Pretrains patch-level surface Transformers with masked vector-quantized objectives and evaluates binding, affinity, and mutation effects; HoloProt's superpixels are fixed summaries learned only through downstream supervision.

competitive_landscape.title: AtomSurf: Surface Representation for Learning on Protein Structures
competitive_landscape.difference: Performs layerwise feature sharing between atom/residue graphs and coarsened surfaces and benchmarks the fusion fairly on Atom3D, directly extending HoloProt's one-direction, one-stage surface-to-residue integration.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: HoloProt is a novel multi-scale graph representation connecting protein surface, structure, and sequence, with molecular superpixels providing major memory savings at little or no performance loss.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper implements explicit surface-to-residue edges, evaluates two distinct tasks and hard generalization splits, and shows a 20-region surface summary can retain or improve enzyme accuracy with few parameters.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The explicit graph-surface fusion and molecular-superpixel idea were useful early contributions. Empirical gains are small and protocol-dependent, the sequence scale is mostly residue features rather than modern sequence modeling, and later end-to-end surfaces, geometric pretraining, and layerwise AtomSurf fusion provide stronger efficiency and benchmark evidence.

reviewer_notes: Read all 18 pages, including the incomplete ablation appendix, exact feature/preprocessing stack, baseline-specific tuning restrictions, compute, and the larger-model enzyme result. dMaSIF, GVP, GearNet, Surface-VQMAE, and AtomSurf were checked against primary CVPR/OpenReview records on 2026-08-23.
